physical-intelligence.summary: Builds robot-control models that combine visual understanding, language, and continuous actions across different machines and manipulation tasks.
physical-intelligence.edge: Rich context steers one action model through strategies, demonstrations, and imperfect rollouts.

skild-ai.summary: Builds shared intelligence for diverse robot bodies, learning locomotion and manipulation from teleoperation, human video, and simulation.
skild-ai.edge: Prompts new tasks with video demonstrations while keeping policy weights fixed.

generalist.summary: Trains embodied models on a dedicated interaction-data engine, studying new robot skills from short demonstrations and little adaptation.
generalist.edge: Physical prompts enter a 30-second context; GEN-1.5 emits 100 Hz action trajectories.

dyna.summary: Builds robot foundation models and commercial task systems, using human-video pretraining to improve dexterity and transfer.
dyna.edge: Couples future-video and action prediction, then checks progress against real customer quality bars.

rlwrld.summary: Develops foundation models for dexterous robots, combining visual and language inputs with torque, touch, temporal context, and industrial skill data.
rlwrld.edge: Separate action streams integrate torque, tactile sensing, motion, and memory before skill refinement.

x-square.summary: Builds embodied models and open training tools, investigating executable VLA pretraining and joint future-video/action learning.
x-square.edge: Combines discrete actions, grounded prediction, and continuous flow objectives in one VLA.

figure.summary: Builds humanoids and learned whole-body control for factory logistics and home tasks, integrating hardware, sensing, data collection, and model training.
figure.edge: Pairs a customer-corroborated factory pilot with explicit unfamiliar-home generalization tests.

1x.summary: Develops tendon-driven home humanoids and learned world models, combining initial autonomy with scheduled remote expert assistance.
1x.edge: Backdrivable tendon hands sense contact; learned visual futures become actions through inverse dynamics.
1x.technology: NEO uses tendon-driven actuation and onboard NVIDIA Jetson Thor. Its July 2026 hand report describes 25 force-controlled degrees of freedom, low-ratio backdrivable tendons, and tactile/shear sensing, so the hand supplies contact observations as well as movement. The January world-model system generates task-conditioned visual futures, then an inverse-dynamics model translates predicted movement into actions. Redwood supplies generalist control, with scheduled human Expert Mode for tasks the initial robot cannot perform alone.

evidence.label: Product terms
evidence.text: The order page lists $20,000 early-access ownership or a $499/month subscription and says US deliveries start in 2026. It explicitly describes basic initial autonomy and remote supervision for unfamiliar complex tasks.

evidence.label: Manufacturing, company-reported
evidence.text: The April 30, 2026 factory account says Hayward production has begun and initial robots are prioritized for internal testing. Production-capacity targets and reserved preorders are not verified consumer deliveries.

evidence.label: Accessible research lineage
evidence.text: Its 2024 World Model Challenge released over 100 hours of vector-quantized robot video, starter models, and evaluation code. This earlier challenge is useful research material, not the latest NEO product model.

evidence.label: Hand engineering, attributed
evidence.text: The July 2026 account specifies 22 actuated finger/palm degrees of freedom plus three wrist degrees, approximately 5:1–15:1 transmission ratios, and tactile/shear sensing. It reports hundreds of hands manufactured; this is component production, not confirmed consumer robot deliveries.

1x.caveat: Consumer shipping plans are not proof of completed deliveries. Initial Expert Mode involves a human watching through robot cameras. No independently verified fleet-wide autonomy/intervention rate was found; the public world-model challenge predates the current product stack. Hand performance, reliability-cycle counts, and production capacity are company claims; dexterity demos do not isolate model autonomy.

agility.summary: Builds Digit humanoids and the Arc fleet platform for moving goods through industrial facilities, with customer-confirmed logistics operations.
agility.edge: Commercial tote handling gives a concrete baseline; Digit 5 adds independent motion-safety control.

sunday.summary: Builds Memo, a wheeled home robot, and ACT models trained with gloves that capture human skills in robot-compatible form.
sunday.edge: Robot-matched gloves align human skill capture with the hands and observations used at inference.
